en.headline: Government proposes higher building safety penalties after Tai Po fire
en.dek: Development Bureau paper to LegCo suggests maximum fine of HK$10 million and five years' jail for dangerous works, and a new category for large-scale maintenance.
body: The Development Bureau has proposed tightening the Buildings Ordinance with higher maximum penalties for dangerous building works and the creation of a new regulated category for large-scale building maintenance, in a paper submitted to the Legislative Council.

Under the proposals, works that cause or may cause death, injury or property damage would carry a maximum fine of HK$10 million and five years' imprisonment, up from the current HK$1 million and three years. Use of substandard materials would attract a fine of up to HK$3 million and three years' imprisonment.

Large-scale maintenance works—defined as those involving buildings of four storeys or above with scaffolding covering at least one whole side across four floors—would require a Buildings Department permit before starting, rather than mere notification. An authorised person would need to submit prescribed plans and a supervision plan.

The proposals follow the Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po last November, which killed 168 people. The government aims to introduce the amendment bill in January and bring the changes into force by the middle of 2027.
A finding of bribery or bid-rigging could result in being struck off statutory contractor and consultant registers without a disciplinary hearing and banned for three years.

zh.headline: 政府擬修例提高樓宇安全罰則 大型維修工程需事先許可
zh.dek: 發展局向立法會提交文件，建議危險工程最高罰款1000萬元及監禁五年，並為大型樓宇維修設立新規管類別。
body: 發展局向立法會提交文件，建議修訂《建築物條例》，提高危險建築工程的最高罰則，並為大型樓宇維修工程設立新的規管類別。
建議下，導致或可能導致死亡、受傷或財產損失的工程，最高罰款由現時的100萬元提高至1000萬元，監禁由三年增至五年。使用不合格材料的罰則最高可達罰款300萬元及監禁三年。
大型維修工程——定義為涉及四層或以上樓宇，且棚架覆蓋整面至少四層——將需事先取得屋宇署許可，而非僅作通知。獲授權人士須提交訂明圖則及監督計劃。
有關建議在去年11月大埔宏福苑火災後提出，該火導致168人死亡。政府計劃明年1月提交修例草案，並於2027年中生效。
如發現涉及賄賂或圍標，可在未經紀律聆訊下將有關人士從法定承建商及顧問名冊除名，並禁制三年。
